commitResults.messageTitle: Make auto-scroll converge reliably on every platform
commitResults.messageBody:
ListView.scrollTo only jumps to an estimated position when the target
row is not laid out yet, and retrying it can settle with the row still
outside the viewport, so slower CI runners timed out before the added
contact became visible. Step towards unrealised rows by exact pixel
amounts instead, and check visibility against the settled layout of the
previous pulse so retries never stop while a scroll is still pending.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name invalid contacts and separate startup recovery guidance
commitResults.messageBody:
Startup load errors identified a bad contact only by its position in
the file, so users had to count entries to find, for example, the
contact with an invalid email. Include the contact's name when it is
valid, and raise the guidance length bound so the longest named
validation message is not truncated.

The unreadable-data warning also packed the cause, the long backup
path and the recovery steps into one paragraph, and told users to
restart even though reload is supported. Split the dialog into cause,
file-location and recovery paragraphs, and recommend entering reload
or restarting in both the dialog and the result display.

Closes #277
Closes #286

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject lookalike and invisible characters in command input
commitResults.messageBody:
Bug-hunting for #142 found that several Unicode inputs were silently
accepted or misreported:

* Integer.parseInt accepts full-width, Arabic-Indic and other decimal
  digits, so `delete １` deleted contact 1. Indexes now require ASCII
  digits.
* Unicode case mapping turns the Kelvin sign into `k`, so `linK 1 2`
  ran `link`, and `ſtudent`, `ﬆudent` and `guardıan` uppercase to valid
  roles. Command words and roles must now be ASCII.
* Only NBSP and U+3000 triggered the unusual-space hint. Other Unicode
  and zero-width spaces in command words and indexes, such as U+202F
  from copied macOS text, gave misleading errors; they now show the
  hint.
* Addresses accepted unpaired surrogates, which cannot be encoded as
  UTF-8 and were silently saved as `?`, embedded control characters
  such as NUL, and accent marks with no base character. These are now
  rejected; tabs remain allowed.

Add regression coverage for lookalike command words, prefixes, roles,
indexes, phones, emails and tags; Unicode and zero-width spaces in
syntax positions; invisible and broken characters in fields and data
files; and null or mistyped JSON values. Lookalike names from other
scripts remain valid, distinct contacts, as documented.

Update the UG, DG and changelog to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Escape brackets in tags shown by add/edit/delete confirmations
commitResults.messageBody:
Confirmation messages concatenated each tag's bracketed name, so a
single tag such as "first][second" displayed exactly like the two tags
"first" and "second". The detailed view already escaped literal
backslashes and square brackets for unambiguous boundaries.

Share that escaping through Messages.formatTag and use it for the
confirmation format too. Tags without backslashes or brackets display
exactly as before, and the detailed view's output is unchanged.

Closes #268

commitResults.messageTitle: Size the load-failure dialog against its target width
commitResults.messageBody:
During a resize the stage width updates before the scene, so measuring
the dialog pane underestimated how tall the wrapped labels become and
the content could overflow the scene, hiding the OK button. Compute the
required height from the stage's target width using remembered window
decorations, and refit when the height drops below the minimum.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe window and screen bounds when fit assertions fail
commitResults.messageBody:
The window-fit assertions only reported that a bound was exceeded, so
platform-specific CI failures gave no sizes to work from. Include the
stage, scene and visual bounds in the failure message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reposition the load-failure dialog using its requested sizes
commitResults.messageBody:
The X/Y clamps read the stage's width and height straight after
requesting new sizes, but those properties update asynchronously on
Windows and macOS, so the window was positioned for its old, smaller
size and its bottom edge could end up off screen.

commitResults.messageTitle: Print full test failure details in Gradle output
commitResults.messageBody:
The window-fit tests fail only on CI platforms, but the default test
logging hides the assertion message that names the offending sizes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Include measured dialog sizes in fit-assertion failures
commitResults.messageBody:
CI-only failures need the remembered decorations, preferred heights
and scroller sizes to identify which measurement is wrong.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refit the load-failure dialog once its scene is laid out
commitResults.messageBody:
The first fit can run before the scene reports a size, so decorations
are unknown and the window ends up one title bar too short; queue a
one-shot refit for when the scene has settled. Restore the height floor
synchronously because some platforms do not clamp programmatic resizes.
Make the fit tests wait, with paced retries, until the dialog's
asynchronous self-correction lands before asserting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover the pre-layout fit path and bound layout refits
commitResults.messageBody:
The fallback used when the recovery viewport has no size yet was never
exercised, failing the patch-coverage check. Exercise it with a direct
fit on an unshown dialog, and bound the pre-layout refit chain so an
unshown stage cannot queue refits forever.
